correctness.rationale: For each Frobenius-normalized plane member the spectral/trace excess and Cauchy--Schwarz bound all singular values in [1-3N eps,1+eps]. Applying this to A,B,(A+B)/sqrt(2) yields the symmetric cross-Gram bound. The skew polar correction J=K(I-H²)^(-1/2) is valid because ||H||<=0.15 and H,K commute; it is real orthogonal and skew. Norm accounting gives the explicit 3,33,34 coefficients. A two-level block-skew family has exact R(E_t)=1+t/(m-1) by monotonicity and normalized spectral spread yielding the lower N eps/4 witness. The derivation holds for every even N>=4 with no reliance on finite sampling; the checker passes 42 diagnostics.

originality.rationale: The known penultimate Gelfand number fixes only the optimal value; the complete two-by-two Grassmannian landscape covers matrix order two only. The new claim is an explicit order-optimal perturbative normal form of every near-minimizing real square two-plane for all even matrix orders at least four, with a matching N-times-excess lower witness. Full relevant public published-finding corpus results and three primary arXiv articles were inspected. An unindexed equivalent quantitative theorem remains possible.
residual_risks: An older theorem about almost orthogonal matrix pencils or quantitative Clifford-module rigidity may be indexed under terminology absent from these searches.
The coefficient 34 is a safe explicit estimate, not an optimal leading numerical coefficient.
Matrix order two is already covered by a stronger exact landscape theorem and is deliberately outside the new claim.

value.rationale: In contrast to the previously known penultimate scalar width, the result completely and quantitatively controls all nearly optimal two-planes by explicit near-Clifford correction, with a constructive counterfamily proving optimal dependence on dimension and excess. The norming-plane stability question is natural for robust matrix subspace design and width extremizer geometry. The result is neither a routine scalar-width corollary nor a numerically isolated example, and it does not claim the elementary polar ingredients as new.
